title: fix: prevent deleting replacement sessions after list refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes bulk Delete targeting a replacement session after the Sessions list refreshes while an older session with the same key remains selected.

## User Impact

Selections survive paging, but a disappeared, filtered-out, replaced, or unverifiable session is deselected after a completed refresh. A replacement does not inherit an earlier selection, including while the deletion confirmation is open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page previously retained only session keys and looked up deletion targets later. It now captures the selected session's identity and archive facts, reconciles selections against completed roster snapshots, and rechecks the captured selection after confirmation. The existing Gateway `expectedSessionId` fence remains authoritative. Pending lifecycle changes retain selections for rollback.

Selection transformations live in a small adjacent module; the page owns the sole selection map. No RPC, storage, or permission contract changes.

## Evidence

- Mounted Sessions page with the real `SessionCapability`: original replacement, removal, and archive cases failed before repair. Missing-ID refresh and deferred-confirmation races also failed before their repairs. Final assertions verify completed deletions, empty errors, and surviving replacements.
- All 76 tests across the selection, lifecycle, archive, roster, and typing files passed in 11.13 seconds with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <five files> --maxWorkers=1`. The six new mounted cases took 88–151 ms each, 715 ms total test-body time.
- CI caught one missed test migration: the Gateway-replacement fixture still assigned the removed key-only selection property. Its original 21-case file reproduced the failure, then passed after migrating the fixture to captured session identities (4.19 seconds). Both Node and Bun CI failures had that same cause. Production and screenshot source remained unchanged; scoped lint and fresh review passed.
- UI production and canonical UI-pages test type checks, scoped lint/stylelint, formatting, i18n verification, line/max-line ratchets, and assertion-safety checks passed. Independent P0–P2 review is clean.
- Real Chromium with identical synthetic Gateway data and matching source snapshots: before 5.69 seconds, after 5.44 seconds. Paging, roster refresh, selected count, and checkbox states verified; neither capture issued a delete request. No live user session was deleted.

The before/after screenshots below show the replacement losing the old checkbox selection while Budget notes remains selected.

![Before: replacement remains checked, two sessions selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2201c11-0cd4-4924-bc8d-a541a139dbcf)

![After: replacement is unchecked, Budget notes remains selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8e5805f-efaa-4554-a082-191c1076aac7)
The hosted review also caught an existing Chromium bulk-delete expectation that conflicted with deselection after refresh. Its original registered case failed waiting for a delete request after the replacement appeared. The existing case now leaves the UI unrefreshed through confirmation, verifies the captured expectedSessionId and visible Gateway stale-identity rejection, then refreshes and verifies the replacement is unchecked. Mounted regressions cover refresh during confirmation; retained Chromium proof verified both orderings. The registered suite retains its original six cases, avoiding an additional browser boot. No production code changed during these fixture corrections.

Final validation: all six existing Chromium deletion cases pass in 25.58 seconds wall (the retained bulk-confirm case is 7.07 seconds). The gateway-context replacement fixture passes all 21 tests in 4.19 seconds. Scoped review is clean, and both owning test-type graphs pass.
